key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation triggers different solid-state conversion pathways in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskites, so bandgap control must be tailored to the specific precursor stack chemistry.
engineering_relevance: These conversion rules enabled the first evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell and provide a scalable solvent-free route to tune absorber bandgaps for high-efficiency tandem manufacturing.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated WBG and NBG precursor stacks
Comparison of solid-state conversion, FA penetration, and halide/Sn-Pb redistribution during annealing
Guided absorber optimization to span 1.26–1.96 eV and build an all-evaporated tandem device
evidence_signal: The optimized evaporated tandem achieved 19.2% power conversion efficiency and retained about 80% of initial efficiency after 1,200 h at 65 °C under ISOS-D-2 testing.
watch_item: Vertical composition gradients in the NBG absorber indicate that interdiffusion and phase reorganization are not fully equilibrated, which could affect long-term uniformity and reproducibility.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
